name: refinement-per-defect-domain
body:
REFINEMENT — per-defect domain coverage [with user, mapping; autonomous, open-question notes].

Problem: all eight requirements drove the single aggregate `domain.group.graph-identity`, which `realised-by` only `solution.component.identity-layer`, `solution.component.scan-driver` and the containers `solution.container.{ts-frontend,java-frontend,py-frontend}`. The per-defect components were therefore ORPHANED — no requirement reached `java-package-hierarchy`, `python-module-identity`, or `ts-package-rooting`, and `domain.entity.runtime-artifact` did not realise `solution.container.go-frontend`.

Resolution — each defect now has its own domain entity realising its own component, and its requirement drives that entity:
- java-default-package-identity → domain.entity.java-package → solution.component.java-package-hierarchy → (contains) solution.container.java-frontend
- python-namespace-package-identity → domain.entity.python-module → solution.component.python-module-identity → (contains) solution.container.py-frontend
- frontend-rooting-from-repo-base → domain.entity.typescript-package → solution.component.ts-package-rooting → (contains) solution.container.ts-frontend
- no-self-ingestion keeps domain.entity.runtime-artifact, which now also `realised-by` solution.container.go-frontend (its component children go-build-cache / scan-hygiene already reached it)
- repo-relative-file-identity additionally drives domain.entity.source-file (the concrete file entity that realises identity-layer), so it no longer routes only through the aggregate group.
The three new entities are contained by domain.group.graph-identity. The now-redundant blanket `realised-by` from domain.group.graph-identity to solution.container.{java,py,ts}-frontend was dropped: the container connection for each defect now comes through its own entity → component → contains → container. Six requirements still carry a `drives` → domain.group.graph-identity edge, and they divide into two groups. Four of them — absolute-paths-at-tool-boundary, frontend-rooting-from-repo-base, java-default-package-identity, python-namespace-package-identity — now also drive their own specific entity (respectively domain.entity.tool-path-resolution, domain.entity.typescript-package, domain.entity.java-package, domain.entity.python-module), so for those the aggregate group is a secondary route alongside a specific defect entity. The remaining two — fast-project-start and repo-relative-file-identity — have identity-layer / scan-driver as a genuine target: fast-project-start drives the aggregate group alone, while repo-relative-file-identity drives it alongside domain.entity.source-file. The containment tree and the existing drives of the four non-defect requirements were otherwise left intact.

Open questions — resolved or explicitly noted:
- User linkage (vocabulary gap): requirements.user.graph-consumer has no `contains` parent under requirements.stakeholder.multi-user-repo-team. The authored vocabulary defines Stakeholder ⊃ Requirement, not Stakeholder ⊃ User, so no valid edge expresses the sub-stakeholder relation. Recorded as a gap; the User stands alone and reaches the requirement tree through the requirement tree itself, not through the stakeholder.
- Value cannot be a `realised-by` source: domain.value.{canonical-file-identity,module-identity,repo-relative-path} are Values, so the write-time matrix forbids them as `realised-by` sources. That is precisely why each defect needs an ENTITY (java-package, python-module, typescript-package) as the domain→component bridge; the Values remain the driven conceptual values.
- Missing bare Java struct: `java.CallGraphBuilder` does NOT resolve in the scanned graph (confirmed empty). The Java component anchors on the real symbols `java.CallGraphBuilder.main` and `java.CallGraphBuilder.Collector.emitPkgHierarchy`.
- C# FQN rendering: the C# frontend renders the language-rooted `csharp.Apg.CsharpFrontend` (not `csharp.CsharpFrontend`). This change-set has no C# defect requirement or node, so no anchor was added; recorded so future anchors use the correct FQN.

Addendum [with user] — tool-boundary coverage (feedback-1): `requirements.requirement.absolute-paths-at-tool-boundary` asserted suite-tool behaviour that no solution node owned; it routed only to the aggregate group and `solution.component.identity-layer`, which explicitly disclaims the tool boundary. It now drives its own entity `domain.entity.tool-path-resolution` (contained by domain.group.graph-identity), which `realised-by` `solution.component.tool-path-resolution` (contained by the new container `solution.container.opencode-suite`, itself contained by solution.system.apg). The component is `implemented-by` the real suite-plumbing anchors `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.findApgRoot` and `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.runCypher` — the shared root-discovery and query boundary every curated tool funnels through. The requirement therefore no longer routes only through the aggregate group and identity-layer. (The sentence above grouping absolute-paths-at-tool-boundary with the requirements whose real target is identity-layer/scan-driver is thereby corrected.)
